answer.label: Michelangelo's idea — modern wording
answer.sourceLine: The idea is Michelangelo's, but this is a modern English rewording. John Addington Symonds quotes a 1548 letter to his nephew Lionardo: “I was never either sculptor or painter in the way of one who keeps a shop.”

author.name: Michelangelo
author.heading: About Michelangelo
author.bio: Michelangelo's career ranged from sculpture to the Sistine Chapel ceiling and architectural commissions. His letters also show him guarding his name and family's social standing, including his objection to being addressed as a shopkeeping craftsman.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: In the fuller letter, Michelangelo objects to a form of address and invokes his family's honor while distinguishing papal service from keeping a shop. Symonds's account ↗ gives the social-status context that disappears when the sentence is reduced to a general statement about artistic independence.
